title: China's CXMT Sees Third-Quarter Revenue Surge of Up to 619%
source_used: Seoul Economic Daily (citing Star Market Daily and Yicai)
key_facts: CXMT, a DRAM maker challenging Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, issued a preliminary earnings announcement on 16 Oct 2026 (reported by Star Market Daily and Yicai on 17 Oct).
Third-quarter revenue is estimated at 114.7 billion to 119.7 billion yuan, up 589 to 619 percent from a year earlier and 15 to 20 percent from the second quarter.
First-three-quarter revenue is expected at 265 billion to 270 billion yuan, up about 725 to 741 percent from 32.1 billion yuan.
Net profit for the first three quarters is expected at 131 billion to 132.5 billion yuan, against a net loss of 5.3 billion yuan a year earlier.
CXMT said AI computing demand rose rapidly since the second half of last year, supply failed to keep pace and prices rose sharply.
Chairman Zhu Yiming proposed a buyback of 1 billion to 2 billion yuan of shares.
CXMT raised up to 66.61 billion yuan in an IPO in July and became the most valuable company on China's mainland exchanges by market capitalisation.
quote_evidence: CXMT said in a preliminary earnings announcement the previous day that third-quarter revenue is estimated at 114.7 billion to 119.7 billion yuan (about 22.9 trillion to 23.9 trillion won), up 589% to 619% from a year earlier.

Separately, CXMT Chairman Zhu Yiming proposed to the company the previous day that it buy back 1 billion to 2 billion yuan (about 200 billion to 400 billion won) worth of its own shares using equity capital or self-raised funds.
why_it_matters_hint: AI-driven memory shortage is lifting a Chinese DRAM challenger; figures are the company's own preliminary range.
notes: AI-translated from Korean. Figures are a preliminary range, unaudited, from the company's own announcement.
